market.method: avg of bottom-up ~65-70 t/yr x ~$3,000/kg = $0.2B and IMARC $0.30B (reports range $0.26-0.44B)
market.job_what: cost of recovering and separating Xe from Kr/air (rare-gas units + cryogenic Kr/Xe purification), world
market.job_method: est.: ~65 t/yr Xe x ~$2,000/kg cost (~2/3 of ~$3,000/kg price; price range $5-20/L = $850-3,400/kg; energy 70-80% of cost) = ~$130M; low confidence

value.logic: only ~1/5 of ~500 big ASUs recover Kr/Xe (retrofit ~EUR80M). Cheap Xe-selective bed on LOX purge at more ASUs: +30 t/yr x $3,000/kg = $90M gross, ~$60M net of their costs
value.margin_logic: MOF/cage sorbent toll-made; sold as packed beds

trend.drivers: 3D NAND and sensor etch, satellite thrusters; lost Ukraine supply; Starlink moved to Kr/Ar

competition.notes: No startup focused on Xe/Kr; MOF makers could enter (NuMat ~$115M raised, Series C ext. 2025). Research leaders: PNNL (SBMOF-1), Liverpool (CC3 cage). Gas majors own the ASUs and the channel.

lab.synth: MOF or porous organic cage, scaled to 10-20 g; 3 variants
lab.test: Xe, Kr, N2, O2, CO2 isotherms at 273/298 K (Micromeritics-type, ~$500-1,200/sample) + humid breakthrough with 400 ppm Xe/40 ppm Kr in air at a university lab
lab.logic: synth 14 wk ~$35k + test 4 wk: 15 isotherms x ~$800 = $12k + breakthrough runs ~$5k

sale.gates: gas-major evaluation; pilot bed on an ASU purge ~1 yr; design-in on new ASUs 2-3 yr; fab Xe-recycle qualification 1-2 yr
